paper_metadata.title: Classification of Financial Data Using Quantum Support Vector Machine

summary: The paper studies quantum-kernel binary classification of a Dhaka Stock Exchange Broad Index dataset using Pauli Y YY and other feature maps on 200-400 samples with 5-7 features. It reports experiments on IBM Quantum simulators and the 7-qubit ibm nairobi QPU, with up to 1024 shots, and claims empirical quantum advantage over classical SVM, but no exact balanced-accuracy or F1 values are given in the text.

experiments.description: Quantum kernel-based binary classification of Dhaka Stock Exchange Broad Index daily trend using the Pauli Y YY feature map, compared against classical SVM across multiple dataset sizes and feature counts on IBM Quantum simulators and IBM hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Support Vector Machine with custom quantum kernels; best-performing Pauli Y YY feature map

hyperparameters.random_seed: single fixed random value for consistency

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are encoded into a quantum feature map circuit; the Pauli Y YY map uses Hadamard layers, single-qubit rotations, and entangling two-qubit interactions parameterized by input features.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of daily changes in the Dhaka Stock Exchange Broad Index using kernelized SVM decision boundaries in quantum feature space.

problem_instance.description: Binary classification of daily changes in the Dhaka Stock Exchange Broad Index, with gold price features merged into the dataset.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Dataset curated by merging historical DSEx Broad Index data from Investing.com with decade-long gold price data from usagold.com; exploratory data analysis performed; random subsets selected for train/test; binary labels predict daily index change.
dataset_specification.train_test_split: random subsets used for training and testing; exact split not reported

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical DSEx Broad Index data merged with gold price data; exploratory data analysis conducted; random subsets of data selected; no noise model used in simulation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Balanced Accuracy and F1 Score used; experiments run across varying dataset sizes and feature counts; comparisons made against classical SVM; 200 separate classical experiments reported for variability analysis; results also checked against PTRI terrain metric.

implementation_details.classical_solver: scikit-learn SVC with precomputed kernel; classical baseline also includes radial basis function kernel SVM
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Kernel computed on quantum circuit, then passed to scikit-learn SVC with precomputed option; direct prediction via scikit-learn predict.

results.uncertainty: equal to number of features; range 5 to 7

speedup_claims.conditions: binary classification of DSEx Broad Index daily trend using custom quantum kernels, especially Pauli Y YY feature map, on dataset sizes 200 to 400 and 5 to 7 features
speedup_claims.caveats: No formal asymptotic speedup is provided; advantage is reported empirically and performance values are not numerically stated in the text.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 7-qubit IBM QPU (ibm nairobi) and qasm simulator; up to 1024 shots; 5-7 features; no asymptotic complexity or crossover analysis reported.
limiting_factors: No numerical performance values for balanced accuracy or F1 are reported in the text
Advantage is empirical and qualitative rather than benchmarked with full statistics
Classical SVM baseline is compared, but the paper does not provide enough quantitative detail to verify superiority rigorously
Small problem sizes (200-400 samples, 5-7 features) and 7-qubit hardware limit practical significance
No formal speedup order or crossover size is given

notes: Hardware reported as IBM Quantum simulators and ibm nairobi QPU; because the paper states both simulation and actual hardware, hardware.type is summarized as simulator_other with device_name ibm nairobi. The paper does not provide asymptotic complexity or a formal speedup order, only empirical quantum advantage claims.

The authors claim empirical quantum advantage and state the Pauli Y YY feature map outperformed classical SVM in most configurations, but the paper does not provide the underlying numeric performance tables in the text excerpt.
